sentence: Atorvastatin is a cholesterol-lowering medicine called a statin.
note: NHS page: type of cholesterol-lowering medicine called a statin.

sentence: The NHS says it is used to treat high cholesterol.
note: Used to treat high cholesterol.

sentence: High cholesterol can cause problems with the heart and blood vessels, known as cardiovascular disease.
note: High cholesterol can cause problems with heart and blood vessels (cardiovascular disease).

sentence: Atorvastatin is also used to help prevent heart disease, including heart attacks and strokes.
note: Also used to prevent heart disease incl. heart attacks and strokes.

sentence: It is only available with a prescription.
note: Only available with a prescription.

sentence: Most people with high cholesterol have no symptoms, so they may not feel any difference after starting it.
note: Summary of common-questions page: may not feel any difference since most people with high cholesterol have no symptoms.

sentence: The NHS says most people take a statin every day for the rest of their life.
note: Returned summary said most people take a statin every day for the rest of their life; summary blended NHS and BHF pages, exact page not identified.

sentence: If someone stops, their cholesterol levels may go up again.
note: How-and-when page summary: if you stop taking it, cholesterol may go up again.

sentence: A doctor decides how much to prescribe, based on why it is needed, the cholesterol level and the other medicines a person takes.
note: Summary: dose depends on reason for taking it, cholesterol levels and other medicines (no figure used).

sentence: Atorvastatin works by stopping the liver from making cholesterol, which lowers the amount of cholesterol in the blood.
note: Summary of common-questions page: stops the liver from making cholesterol, lowering blood cholesterol.

sentence: Statins as a group also help the liver to remove LDL cholesterol that is already in the blood.
note: Statins search summary: reduce cholesterol the liver makes and increase liver's ability to remove LDL already in blood; summary blended NHS 111 Wales and MedlinePlus, page not identified.

sentence: LDL is one of the types of cholesterol carried in the blood.
note: Plain textbook definition.

sentence: The NHS says cholesterol levels should fall within a few weeks if the medicine is taken regularly as prescribed.
note: Summary: levels should drop within about four weeks if taken regularly (number not used); simvastatin page gave the same wording, so attribution to the atorvastatin page is from the summary only.

sentence: The NHS says routine liver blood tests are offered during the first year of treatment.
note: Summary: routine liver blood test scheduled in first year; the pravastatin page said the same, atorvastatin attribution from the summary only.

sentence: The NHS says a person can take atorvastatin with or without food.
note: How-and-when summary: take it with or without food.

sentence: The NHS says taking two doses to make up for a missed one is not advised.
note: Summary: skip the missed dose and take next at usual time; do not take 2 doses to make up.

sentence: The NHS says people should not reduce the amount they take without talking to a doctor first.
note: Summary: do not reduce your dose without talking to your doctor first.

sentence: The NHS lists headache, dizziness, feeling sick, digestive problems, muscle aches and swollen joints, a blocked or runny nose or nosebleeds, and sleep problems as common side effects.
note: Summary of NHS atorvastatin pages: common side effects as listed.

sentence: Serious side effects are uncommon.
note: Serious side effects are uncommon.

sentence: They include inflammation of the liver or pancreas, and inflammation and damage to the muscles.
note: Serious: liver inflammation, pancreas inflammation, muscle inflammation and damage.

sentence: Muscle problems can cause cramps, severe pain and weakness, and sometimes a high temperature and red or brown pee.
note: Summary: muscle cramps, severe pain, weakness; may also have high temperature and red or brown pee.

sentence: The NHS says anyone taking atorvastatin who thinks they may be having serious side effects should call NHS 111.
note: Overview page advice: call NHS 111 if you think you might be having serious side effects.

sentence: Yellowing of the skin or eyes can point to liver problems, and severe stomach pain can point to inflammation of the pancreas.
note: Summary: both listed as serious side effects on NHS pages; exact wording of symptom lines not seen.

sentence: A serious allergic reaction is an emergency: sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, or very fast or difficult breathing, needs a 999 call.
note: Summary: call 999 for swollen lips, mouth, throat, tongue or breathing very fast/struggling.

sentence: The NHS says not to drive to A&E in that situation.
note: Summary: advises not to drive yourself to A&E.

sentence: For other side effects, the NHS says to talk to a doctor first, who can check whether atorvastatin is the cause and may change the amount or the medicine.
note: Summary: talk to doctor first to see if it really is a side effect; doctor may lower dose or change medicine.

sentence: If a side effect happens with one statin, it may not happen with another.
note: Statins search summary; page not identified (blended NHS drug pages).

sentence: Statins can interact with some other medicines, which can raise the risk of serious side effects such as muscle damage.
note: Summaries: statins can interact with other medicines, increasing risk of serious side effects such as muscle damage.

sentence: In that case a doctor may prescribe a different statin or a lower amount of the current one.
note: Summary of NHS 111 Wales/NHS text: alternative statin or lower dosage; page not identified.

sentence: The NHS says to tell the doctor or pharmacist about any other medicines, herbal remedies, vitamins or supplements being taken.
note: Summary: patients should tell their doctor about other medicines, herbal remedies, vitamins or supplements; blended, page not identified.

sentence: The NHS says drinking a lot of grapefruit juice can affect how atorvastatin works.
note: Summary: lots of grapefruit juice can affect the way this medicine works; limit stated as small glasses.

sentence: The British Heart Foundation says grapefruit can be had occasionally with atorvastatin, but not in large quantities.
note: Summary of BHF page.

sentence: The NHS says people can drink alcohol while taking atorvastatin, but regularly drinking a lot raises the chance of side effects such as liver problems.
note: Summary: you can drink, but regularly drinking a lot increases the chance of side effects and liver problems.

sentence: It suggests trying to limit alcohol while taking the medicine.
note: Summary: try to limit how much alcohol you drink.

sentence: Regularly drinking large amounts of alcohol is also on the NHS list of reasons a person may not be suitable for atorvastatin.
note: Who-can-and-cannot summary lists regularly drinking large amounts of alcohol.

sentence: The NHS says most adults can take atorvastatin.
note: Summary: most adults (and children aged 10 and over) can take it; age figure not used.

sentence: It may not suit people who have ever had an allergic reaction to atorvastatin or another medicine, or who have liver or kidney problems.
note: Summary list.

sentence: An underactive thyroid, past muscle side effects from a statin and a history of a muscle disorder, including fibromyalgia, are also on the list.
note: Summary list: underactive thyroid, previous muscular side effects with a statin, muscle disorder incl. fibromyalgia.

sentence: Sources differ on how firmly they advise against statins in liver disease, so this is a decision for the prescriber.
note: Search summary: NHS 111 Wales firmer, MedlinePlus less absolute; 'decision for prescriber' is the author's framing.

sentence: Atorvastatin is not recommended in pregnancy because it can affect how a baby develops.
note: Summary: NHS says not recommended during pregnancy because it can affect how your baby develops.

sentence: The NHS advises stopping it some months before trying to conceive, so anyone planning a pregnancy needs to speak to a doctor or pharmacist.
note: Summary: stop 3 months before trying to conceive (number not used). 'speak to a doctor' is the author's route-to-care wording.

sentence: On breastfeeding, the NHS says a person may be able to take it but should check with a pharmacist or doctor first.
note: Summary: may be able to take while breastfeeding; check first.

sentence: MedlinePlus, a US source, is stricter and says statins should not be taken while pregnant or breastfeeding.
note: Search summary: MedlinePlus says you should not take statins if pregnant or breastfeeding.

sentence: The NHS says drinking a lot of grapefruit juice can affect how atorvastatin works.
note: As in section 4.

sentence: The British Heart Foundation says grapefruit can be had occasionally, but not in large quantities.
note: BHF summary.

sentence: The advice differs between statins, and the NHS says grapefruit juice should be avoided with simvastatin.
note: Statins summary: do not drink grapefruit juice with simvastatin (NHS simvastatin page); not atorvastatin specific.

sentence: A pharmacist or doctor can say what suits an individual.
note: Author's route-to-care sentence; sources say check with pharmacist or doctor generally.

sentence: The NHS says most people take a statin every day for the rest of their life.
note: As above.

sentence: If it is stopped, cholesterol levels may rise again.
note: As above.

sentence: The NHS says to talk to a doctor before stopping, even when side effects are suspected.
note: Summary: talk to your doctor first about side effects.

sentence: The doctor may be able to change the amount or the medicine instead.
note: Summary: doctor may lower dose or change medicine.

sentence: The NHS lists muscle aches among the common side effects of atorvastatin.
note: Common side effects list includes muscle aches and swollen joints.

sentence: More serious muscle inflammation and damage is uncommon.
note: Serious side effects uncommon, include muscle damage.

sentence: Cramps, severe pain or weakness, sometimes with a high temperature and red or brown pee, are reasons for the NHS to say call NHS 111.
note: Overview page: call 111 if you think you might be having serious side effects.

sentence: For milder aches, a talk with the GP is the usual first step.
note: Summary: talk to your doctor first. Routing to a GP appointment is the site's convention, not stated by name in the returned text.

sentence: The NHS says atorvastatin is not recommended in pregnancy because it can affect how a baby develops.
note: As above.

note: As above.

sentence: Anyone who is pregnant or planning a pregnancy needs to speak to a doctor or pharmacist.
note: Author's route-to-care wording.

sentence: Advice on breastfeeding differs between sources, so that too is best discussed with a pharmacist or doctor.
note: NHS: may be able to take it, check first; MedlinePlus: should not.

sentence: Some older leaflets give slightly different wording, so the current NHS page is the one to follow.
